author: SMAC Digital
bodyHtml:
Every morning, thousands of Indian manufacturers, fashion merchants, and lifestyle brand owners open their seller dashboards on platforms like Meesho, Myntra, Flipkart, and Amazon. The graphs look impressive at first glance: hundreds of dispatched parcels, high daily order volumes, and gross sales figures that run into lakhs of rupees.

Yet, when the bi-weekly payout settlement hits their bank account, the celebratory mood evaporates.

After factoring in platform referral cuts, payment handling fees, reverse logistics for customer returns, damaged goods, and platform advertising spends, the net profit is razor-thin. In worse scenarios, sellers find themselves operating at a net loss despite clocking record shipment volumes.

This vicious cycle is known as **The Marketplace Trap**.

While third-party aggregators promise frictionless volume, their algorithmic structures, punitive commission layers, and aggressive discounting mandates drain your business of real cash flow.

If you want to build a business that is genuinely profitable and legally yours for the long term, the solution is not to sell cheaper on someone else's platform. The solution is taking control of your distribution through an **independent Direct-to-Consumer (D2C) Shopify storefront.** Businesses can support this transition with professional website design and development services and strategic SEO services to improve their online presence. Additionally, digital marketing services can help brands reach their target audiences and build awareness for their independent storefronts.

The Illusion of High Sales: Why Big Numbers Aren't Hitting Your Bank Account

Gross merchandise value (GMV) is a vanity metric. What matters at the end of every fiscal month is net cash in bank. Unfortunately, the math of third-party platforms is intentionally structured to disguise where your revenue disappears.

The Hidden Deductions: Referral Fees, Shipping Surcharges, and Reverse Logistics

When you price an item on Myntra or Meesho, you are never just paying a single flat fee. A cascade of micro-deductions chips away at your invoice value:

If even one customer returns that item, the reverse logistics and repackaging costs will wipe out the profit of your next three sales. Sellers are left doing high-stress manual labor for an effective margin that barely covers their office electricity bills.

The Return-to-Origin (RTO) Nightmare: How Unchecked Returns Destroy Thin Margins

Return-to-Origin (RTO) is the single biggest profit killer in Indian e-commerce. On open marketplaces, liberal "no-questions-asked" return windows and zero customer accountability encourage impulsive, non-serious buying.

Customers routinely order three different sizes of the same kurta on Myntra or Meesho, try them on, keep one, and hand two back to the courier. Even worse, on Cash-on-Delivery (COD) orders, consumers frequently reject the parcel at their doorstep simply because they changed their mind or were unavailable.

Who bears the financial brunt of this trial behavior? The seller.

  • You pay the forward delivery shipping fee.
  • You pay the reverse logistics penalty.
  • You absorb transit damages, broken tamper-evident seals, and soiled packaging.

In categories like ethnic apparel, footwear, and home decor, marketplace return rates regularly hover between 25% and 40%. When nearly one out of every three parcels bounces back at your expense, operating profitably on a 15% wholesale margin is mathematically impossible.

To build a more sustainable online business, sellers can invest in a dedicated storefront supported by professional website development services. Improving product-page visibility through SEO services and reaching relevant audiences with digital marketing services can also help independent D2C brands grow their online presence.

The Quality Dilemma: How Ruthless Price Wars Force Sellers to Cut Corners

Beyond immediate cash-flow drainage, marketplaces inflict an even deeper wound: they systematically destroy your product quality and your brand reputation.

Why Marketplace Algorithms Prioritize the Cheapest, Not the Best

Marketplace ranking algorithms are programmed for immediate transaction conversions. They do not care about the thread count of your pure cotton sheets, the grade of your brass hardware, or the environmental safety of your dyes.

The algorithm looks at two primary levers: Conversion Rate and Lowest Price Point.

If a competitor lists an imitation product using synthetic polyester instead of pure handloom cotton and undercuts your price by ?150, the algorithm instantly demotes your listing and promotes theirs. To regain sales velocity, you are forced into an unwinnable "race to the bottom"—slashing your prices, compromising on raw materials, and lowering your production standards just to appear in the search results.

How Competing on Price Slowly Destroys Your Brand Reputation

When you are forced to degrade fabric weight, substitute brass for zinc alloy, or skip quality-control checks, the customer does not blame the marketplace. They blame your product.

Bad reviews pile up, your star ratings drop, and your brand becomes associated with cheap, disposable goods. Once a brand is categorized as "cheap" in the consumer’s mind, you can never command premium prices again. You have traded your long-term reputation for short-term platform survival.

To build a stronger independent brand, businesses can invest in a professional website design strategy that showcases product quality and brand identity. A well-optimized online store supported by search engine optimization can help potential customers discover your products through relevant search queries.

Brands can also use social media marketing services to communicate their craftsmanship, share product stories, and build relationships with their target audience. With the right content marketing strategy, manufacturers can highlight the quality, materials, and value that differentiate their products from cheaper alternatives.

The Direct-to-Consumer Shift: Why Savvy Sellers Are Migrating to Shopify

Direct-to-Consumer (D2C) is not an unproven trend; it is the proven playbook of India's most successful retail brands. Migrating your core catalog to an independent Shopify store fundamentally rewires your business model in three critical ways:

0% Platform Commission: Keeping the Full 20% to 35% in Your Business

Shopify does not operate on a predatory commission model. They provide the software and digital storefront; you keep your earnings.

Outside of standard payment gateway fees (typically around 2% for Razorpay, Cashfree, or Paytm), the full retail price flows straight into your company’s account. That 20% to 35% previously lost to marketplace commissions can now be reinvested directly into:

  • Targeted digital advertising that brings customers straight to your brand.
  • Premium packaging that creates memorable unboxing experiences.
  • Healthy net profit reserves that protect your business during slow seasons.

Full Control Over Return and Replacement Policies

When you own your Shopify store, you set the terms of service—not a third-party platform algorithm.

  • You can replace liberal "return for any reason" policies with a fair "Replacement Only for Transit Damages or Size Exchanges" policy.
  • You can mandate an unboxing video within 24 hours of delivery to eliminate fraudulent claims.
  • You can run OTP-based phone verification on COD checkouts or offer a 5% discount for prepaid orders, slashing your RTO rate from 35% down to under 8%.

Unlocking the Real Goldmine: 100% Ownership of Your Customer Data

When someone buys from you on Meesho or Myntra, you never see their full phone number or direct email address. The customer belongs entirely to the platform.

On Shopify, you own 100% of your first-party customer data. Every name, delivery address, phone number, and purchase preference is securely logged in your database.

This database is a tangible financial asset. Over two years, building a list of 25,000 verified customers means you can launch new collections, announce flash sales, or drive festival purchases with a single broadcast message—without paying a single rupee in marketplace referral fees.

Key Shopify Features Marketplaces Will Never Offer You

A custom Shopify store does not just match the shopping experience of major marketplaces—it gives you specialized enterprise tools that marketplaces intentionally keep for themselves:

Automated Abandoned Cart and Checkout Recovery

Across the e-commerce industry, nearly 70% of shoppers add products to their cart but leave before completing payment. On marketplaces, you have zero recourse when this happens.

On Shopify, intelligent automation immediately triggers:

  • An automated WhatsApp alert within 15 minutes: "Hey [Name], you left your favorite handcrafted bedsheet in your cart! Complete your order now and enjoy an extra 5% off."
  • Automated recovery email sequences that recover between 15% and 25% of lost checkouts automatically while you sleep.

Seamless WhatsApp & SMS Integrations for Zero-Cost Repeat Orders

In India, commerce moves on WhatsApp. Shopify integrates seamlessly with WhatsApp Business API tools like Wati, Interakt, and Quickirr:

  • Send instant order confirmation messages with live tracking links.
  • Run automated post-purchase surveys and loyalty point updates.
  • Broadcast festive catalog releases directly to customers' WhatsApp chats, producing immediate sales spikes with zero paid ad spend.

Global Selling Ready: Multi-Currency and International Checkout

Selling on Myntra or Meesho restricts you primarily to domestic, price-sensitive shoppers. But handcrafted items, Indian ethnic textiles, and artisanal decor enjoy enormous demand overseas.

Through Shopify Markets, your store is instantly export-ready:

  • Automatically detects the visitor’s country and displays prices in USD, GBP, EUR, or AED.
  • Calculates international shipping duties and taxes at checkout.
  • Integrates with global payment engines like PayPal, Stripe, and international credit cards, allowing you to sell a product for $85 overseas that fetches only ?1,800 domestically.

The Winning Hybrid Playbook: Turn Marketplace Buyers into Direct Store Fans

Escaping the marketplace trap does not mean you must delete your Meesho or Myntra seller accounts tomorrow morning. The smartest brand owners use a Hybrid Funnel Strategy:

Using Marketplaces for Initial Discovery, Not Long-Term Loyalty

Treat marketplaces as paid discovery engines rather than your primary business home.

  • List your mass-market, lower-margin introductory products on Meesho or Myntra to capture initial eyeballs.
  • Keep your premium, high-margin, signature collections exclusively on your Shopify store.
  • Use the sheer volume of marketplaces simply to identify new buyers, with the explicit goal of moving them onto your own platform for every subsequent purchase.

Smart Packaging Inserts and Exclusive First-Order Store Discounts

Every single box leaving your dispatch facility must contain a branded physical touchpoint:

  • The Welcome Envelope: An unboxing card printed on textured paper detailing the artisan story behind your workshop.
  • The Irresistible Offer: "Thank you for your purchase! Register your product warranty and get ?300 OFF your next purchase by ordering directly from our official website:smacdigital
  • The QR Code Bridge: A scannable QR code that opens an automated WhatsApp welcome flow, instantly capturing the buyer's phone number and handing them a direct checkout link.

By turning anonymous marketplace shoppers into registered direct customers, you convert expensive one-off orders into high-lifetime-value brand relationships.

Scale Your D2C Brand with SMAC Digital

Building an independent e-commerce brand requires more than choosing a pre-made theme. It demands thoughtful technical architecture, conversion rate optimization, and seamless backend operational integrations.

That is where SMAC Digital comes in.

From Strategy to Launch: Complete Shopify Store Development

At SMAC Digital, we specialize in helping traditional manufacturers, craft enterprises, and growing retail brands break free from third-party marketplace dependencies:

  • Bespoke UI/UX Design: Custom storefronts that look and feel like premium lifestyle brands, built mobile-first for lightning-fast loading speeds on Indian mobile networks.
  • Turnkey Tech Integrations: Full setup of domestic payment gateways (Razorpay, Cashfree, UPI), automated shipping aggregators (Shiprocket, Delhivery), and ERP systems.
  • Conversion Optimization (CRO): Streamlined 1-step checkouts, dynamic upsells, and trust badges engineered to maximize conversion rates and minimize drop-offs.
  • RTO Defense Systems: Setup of automated COD-to-Prepaid conversion flows and address verification tools to keep delivery failure rates to an absolute minimum.

Get a Free E-Commerce Consultation with SMAC Digital

Stop watching your hard-earned margins get swallowed by 30% platform commissions, return fraud, and unfair price cuts. Take ownership of your customers, your pricing, and your future.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

1. Isn't it cheaper to sell on Meesho because they claim zero percent commission on some categories?

While platforms like Meesho advertise "0% commission" on specific entry-level catalogs, the true cost of selling is hidden in logistical overhead. Return-to-Origin (RTO) charges, reverse shipping penalties, customer dispute fees, and compulsory advertising credits significantly erode seller earnings. Furthermore, you gain zero customer data, leaving you perpetually dependent on platform promotions to generate volume.

2. How much does it cost to build and run an independent Shopify store?

title: From Wholesaler to D2C: How Home Decor & Handicraft Manufacturers Can Double Margins and Build Long-Term Brand Value with Shopify
excerpt: The bustling industrial sectors of Sitapura, Vishwakarma (VKI), Sanganer, and Bagru tell a familiar story. Warehouses overflow with hand-carved Sheesham furniture, solid brass artifacts, hand-knotted rugs, and intricate block-printed textiles. The...
author: SMAC Digital
bodyHtml:
The bustling industrial sectors of Sitapura, Vishwakarma (VKI), Sanganer, and Bagru tell a familiar story. Warehouses overflow with hand-carved Sheesham furniture, solid brass artifacts, hand-knotted rugs, and intricate block-printed textiles. The level of craftsmanship and production capacity coming out of Indian manufacturing hubs is world-class.

Yet, when you look at the balance sheets of many manufacturers, the story takes an unsettling turn: soaring top-line turnover, but paper-thin net profit margins.

For decades, traditional manufacturers have relied almost exclusively on B2B wholesaling, third-party exporters, and aggregator platforms like IndiaMART, Meesho, and Myntra. While these avenues once provided dependable volume, the commercial reality has changed drastically. Today, rising raw material costs, unpredictable platform fees, and relentless price wars are squeezing producers to their breaking point.

To survive and thrive over the next decade, forward-thinking manufacturers are making a critical shift: transitioning from anonymous wholesale suppliers into Direct-to-Consumer (D2C) brands powered by independent Shopify storefronts. Businesses can strengthen this transition with professional website design and development services and a well-planned digital strategy.

In this comprehensive guide, we unpack why the traditional wholesale model is hitting a ceiling, the exact financial mechanics of doubling your margins with D2C, and how building an independent digital storefront creates a resilient, multi-million-dollar brand asset for the long run. Effective SEO services and digital marketing solutions can also help D2C brands improve their online visibility and reach potential customers.

 

The Wholesaler’s Ceiling: Why Relying Only on B2B and Marketplaces Limits Long-Term Growth

Traditional business models provided stability during simpler times, but they carry an invisible structural ceiling that prevents manufacturers from capturing the true value of their work.

The IndiaMART & Aggregator Trap: Competing Exclusively on Price

When you list your products on B2B directories like IndiaMART or sell via open marketplaces like Meesho, the platform architecture inherently commoditizes you. Prospective buyers are placed on a screen where your meticulously hand-hammered brass planter is shown right beside five cheap, machine-stamped alternatives.

In this environment, buyer psychology is conditioned entirely around one question: "Who has the lowest quote?"

There is no room to talk about artisan provenance, material longevity, or the three-generation legacy behind your casting techniques. You are forced to shave your prices down to pennies just to secure the deal. If you raise your prices by even 5%, the buyer simply moves to the next listing.

Thin Margins vs. Rising Raw Material & Labor Costs

Over the past five years, the baseline cost of running a production unit has skyrocketed. Seasoned timber, copper, brass, organic cotton dyes, and skilled artisan wages have climbed steadily.

When you operate on fixed 10%–15% wholesale margins, even a slight fluctuation in logistics or raw material prices completely wipes out your profit. You end up shouldering 100% of the operational risk, while middlemen, retail distributors, and aggregator platforms take the lion's share of the final consumer markup.

Building Someone Else’s Platform Instead of Your Own Long-Term Business Asset

Here is the uncomfortable truth: every order fulfilled through a retail broker or a third-party marketplace is helping them build an asset, not you.

When a customer orders a set of block-printed curtains on Myntra, they do not consider themselves your customer; they are Myntra’s customer. Myntra keeps their contact information, learns their preferences, and uses that data to cross-sell competitors' products tomorrow. You are merely an interchangeable fulfillment node in someone else's supply chain.

Doubling Net Margins: The Immediate Math of Direct-to-Consumer (D2C)

Switching to D2C is not merely a branding exercise; it is an immediate financial upgrade to your bottom line.

The Breakdown: Where Does the Money Actually Go?

To understand why direct commerce transforms your factory’s balance sheet, look at the cold numbers comparing an identical product under both business models:

1. The Traditional Wholesale Model (High Volume, Vanishing Margins)

  • Manufacturing Cost: ?800
  • Wholesale Selling Price: ?1,050
  • Your Net Margin: ?250 per unit
  • Final Retail Shelf Price: ?2,800 to ?3,500

In this setup, your factory absorbs 100% of the production risk, inventory financing, artisan wages, and workshop overhead—yet you walk away with just ?250. The distribution chain (distributors, stockists, and retail showrooms) captures between ?1,750 and ?2,450 of gross margin on the product you manufactured.

If fuel or raw material costs increase by even 10%, your entire ?250 margin is instantly erased.

2. The Direct-to-Consumer (Shopify) Model (Full Margin Capture)

  • Manufacturing Cost: ?800
  • D2C Retail Selling Price: ?2,600 (more competitive than showroom prices)
  • Paid Ads & Courier/Logistics: ?750
  • Your Net Take-Home: ?1,050 per unit
     

By selling directly through your own branded Shopify store:

  • You undercut expensive luxury retail showrooms (pricing at ?2,600 instead of ?3,500), offering exceptional value to the end consumer.
  • You comfortably absorb performance marketing and pan-India doorstep delivery costs (?750).
  • Your take-home profit increases from ?250 to ?1,050—a massive 4.2x increase in pure net cash flow per order.

The Big Takeaway for Manufacturers

To make ?1,05,000 in net profit:

  • In the Wholesale Model, you have to produce, pack, and distribute 420 units.
  • In the Shopify D2C Model, you only need to sell 100 units.

That means 75% less raw material consumed, 75% less factory labor strain, zero dependency on delayed B2B payment cycles, and you build a direct base of 100 happy customers who will buy again next season at zero customer acquisition cost.

Packaging Authentic Craftsmanship as a Premium Lifestyle Choice

Consumers in metropolitan cities (Mumbai, Bengaluru, Delhi NCR) and affluent international markets do not want nameless, mass-produced decor. They actively seek character, warmth, and authenticity.

When you control your own website, you are not trapped in a rigid grid of identical marketplace cards. You have the canvas to showcase:

  • High-definition video showing the metal spinning and hand-etching process.
  • The story of the master artisans crafting the piece.
  • Styling suggestions demonstrating how the piece transforms a contemporary living room.

Storytelling bridges the gap between a commodity and a luxury lifestyle artifact, allowing you to comfortably command premium retail pricing without pushback.

Turning Single-Item Buyers into High-Average-Order-Value (AOV) Customers

On marketplaces, customers buy one isolated product and leave. On an independent Shopify store, you control the entire merchandising experience.

Using intelligent bundle apps, cross-sells, and tiered discounts (e.g., "Complete the Look: Add Matching Brass Candle Holders for 15% off"), home decor brands routinely elevate their Average Order Value (AOV) from ?1,200 to over ?3,800 per transaction.

Building a Resilient, Long-Term Business Asset (Why D2C Wins Over the Next 10 Years)

A wholesale operation is often valued only on physical machinery and raw warehouse inventory. A direct-to-consumer brand, however, commands a true company enterprise valuation.

Marketplace Storefront vs. Independent Brand: Which One Holds Real Valuation?

If an investor, private equity firm, or buyer looks at your enterprise:

  • A business with ?10 Crore in revenue on Meesho/Amazon is viewed as high-risk. Why? Because the platform could alter its ranking algorithm, introduce a private-label clone, or suspend the seller account overnight.
  • A business with ?10 Crore in revenue on an independent Shopify store is an enterprise asset. You possess proprietary traffic, direct customer access, repeat brand search volume, and defensible brand equity.

Protecting Your Intellectual Property, Design Exclusivity, and Artisan Heritage

Every manufacturer has experienced this frustration: you spend months developing an original, innovative furniture or textile pattern. Within four weeks of listing it on a marketplace, five competing sellers copy your photos, clone your design using sub-par materials, and undercut your price.

With your own branded storefront, your unique design collections remain protected under your brand umbrella. You dictate the presentation, safeguard your creative work, and build an exclusive customer following that respects genuine design.

Immunity Against Sudden Platform Policy Changes, Account Suspensions, and Fee Hikes

Third-party marketplaces periodically update their fee structures, increase shipping charges, or tighten return windows with zero seller input. Waking up to an algorithm change that cuts your listing visibility by 70% can cripple a factory overnight.

Owning your Shopify infrastructure means you own your digital real estate. Nobody can de-list your best-selling product or throttle your visibility.

Maximizing Customer Lifetime Value (LTV): The True Engine of Long-Term Wealth

The real profitability in e-commerce does not come from the first sale; it comes from the second, third, and fourth purchases where your customer acquisition cost (CAC) drops to zero.

100% First-Party Customer Data: Building Your Permanent Buyer Database

Every order placed on Shopify delivers verified first-party data: customer names, shipping addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, and specific purchasing behaviors.

This data is your company’s greatest digital asset. Over three to five years, a customer database of 50,000 to 100,000 verified decor buyers becomes a perpetual revenue engine that no competitor can touch.

Zero-Cost Festive Remarketing via WhatsApp, SMS, and Email Automations

When festival seasons arrive—Diwali, New Year, wedding seasons—marketplace sellers must bid aggressive sums on sponsored ads just to get their own past customers to look at their products.

With a dedicated store, automated flows do the heavy lifting at negligible cost:

  • Automated Abandoned Cart Flows: Recover 15%–25% of uncompleted checkouts via WhatsApp alerts.
  • Segmented Festive Broadcasts: Send exclusive catalog previews to your top 20% highest-spending customers.
  • Post-Purchase Follow-Ups: Trigger automated care instructions (e.g., "How to care for your solid brass decor") followed by a complementary product suggestion 14 days later.

Creating Loyal Brand Advocates Who Never Ask for Marketplace Discounts

When customers develop an emotional connection to your aesthetic, your packaging, and your unboxing experience, they stop looking for discounts. They become brand loyalists who proudly tag your products on Instagram and recommend your brand by name to friends and family.

Why Shopify is the Ideal Platform for Long-Term Scaling

Shopify powers over 4 million businesses worldwide, including top Indian and global decor brands, because it is engineered specifically for direct commerce.

Visual Storytelling & Immersive Lookbooks Built for Decor and Artisanal Products

Home decor is deeply visual and emotional. Shopify’s ecosystem allows brands to build:

  • "Shop the Room" Interactive Features: Let buyers click directly on a styled living room photo to purchase the rug, lamp, and cushion covers together.
  • High-Res Zoom & 3D AR Models: Allow buyers to see the exact texture of handloom fabric or preview a brass statue on their console table using augmented reality.

Frictionless Global Expansion: Selling in USD, EUR, and GBP at 3x to 5x Domestic Margins

Handicrafts and Indian home decor command immense value in overseas markets like the United States, United Kingdom, Australia, and the UAE. A wooden carving or hand-block bedspread that sells for ?2,500 in India frequently commands $90 to $140 (?7,500 to ?11,500) abroad.

Through Shopify Markets, international selling is built into the core:

  • Automatic local currency display and checkout.
  • Calculation of duties and taxes at checkout.
  • Multi-language support and international payment gateways (PayPal, Stripe, international credit cards).

Scalable Architecture: Smooth Operations from 10 Orders a Day to 10,000

You never need to worry about server crashes during festive sales spikes. Shopify provides 99.99% uptime, bank-grade security, and seamless connections with major Indian logistics aggregators (Shiprocket, Delhivery, Bluedart) and ERP systems.

Why Is Mobile App Development Important for Businesses?

Mobile applications make it easier for customers to access services, explore products, communicate with businesses, and complete transactions. A well-designed app can also improve customer engagement and streamline business operations.

Here are some key benefits of business mobile app development:

  • Better customer experience: Provide convenient access to your products and services.

  • Improved efficiency: Automate selected business processes and workflows.
  • Increased accessibility: Allow customers to interact with your business from their smartphones.
  • Business growth: Create additional opportunities for customer retention and revenue generation.

A successful application should solve a real customer problem rather than simply add another digital channel.

1. Understand Your Business Requirements

Before hiring a mobile application development company, define what you want your app to achieve. Consider your target audience, essential features, preferred platforms, and business objectives.

For example, an e-commerce business may need product listings, secure payments, order tracking, and customer accounts. A service-based company may require appointment booking, notifications, and customer support features.

A clear project scope helps your development partner recommend appropriate technologies and estimate costs more accurately.

2. Check Experience and Technical Expertise

The right development partner should understand the technical requirements of your project and have experience building applications with similar functionality.

When evaluating a mobile app development agency, consider its experience with:

  • Android and iOS platforms
  • User interface and user experience design
  • API integration
  • Database management
  • Application security
  • Performance optimization
  • Testing and maintenance

Reviewing previous projects and case studies can help you assess whether a company is suitable for your business requirements.

Your target audience should influence your platform choice.

Android app development services can help businesses reach users across a broad range of Android devices. An experienced iOS app development company can build applications designed for Apple's mobile ecosystem.

Depending on your budget and audience, you may choose Android, iOS, or a cross-platform solution. Discuss the advantages, limitations, development costs, and ongoing maintenance requirements before making a decision.

4. Choose Custom Mobile App Development

Every business has different operational needs, so a ready-made application may not always provide the flexibility you require.

Custom mobile app development allows businesses to build features around their specific workflows, customers, and goals. This can include customer dashboards, payment gateways, booking systems, inventory management, or third-party integrations.

Professional custom app development services should also consider scalability, security, usability, and future upgrades. A well-planned application can adapt as your business grows.

5. Compare Mobile App Development Services and Costs

Price is an important consideration, but choosing the cheapest provider may not deliver the best long-term value.

When comparing mobile app development services Jaipur, request a clear project proposal covering:

  • Project scope and deliverables
  • UI/UX design
  • Development and testing
  • Third-party integrations
  • Deployment and launch
  • Maintenance and technical support

A transparent estimate helps you understand where your budget will be spent and reduces the risk of unexpected costs.

6. Prioritize User Experience and App Security

A mobile application should be easy to navigate, responsive, and reliable. Complicated menus, slow loading times, and confusing checkout processes can discourage users from continuing.

Your development partner should focus on intuitive navigation, accessible design, efficient performance, and thorough testing.

Security is equally important. Depending on your app, suitable safeguards may include secure authentication, encrypted data transmission, appropriate access controls, and regular updates.

7. Consider Long-Term Support and Maintenance

Launching an app is only the beginning. Operating systems change, devices receive updates, and users expect new features and improvements.

Before choosing a mobile application development company, clarify how it handles bug fixes, compatibility updates, performance monitoring, and ongoing support.

Reliable maintenance helps keep your application functional, secure, and aligned with changing business requirements.

Search is changing rapidly. Users are no longer relying only on traditional Google results; they are increasingly asking AI platforms for direct answers, recommendations, comparisons, and solutions. What Is AI Search Optimization?

AI search optimization is the process of structuring and improving website content so that AI-powered search systems can understand, interpret, and potentially use it when generating answers.

Traditional SEO primarily focuses on improving visibility in search engine result pages. AI search engine optimization, on the other hand, also considers how content can provide clear answers to conversational and contextual queries.

This includes optimizing:

  • Website content
  • Headings and subheadings
  • FAQs
  • Structured information
  • Entity relationships
  • Author and business information
  • Helpful, original answers

AI Search vs Traditional SEO: What's the Difference?

Understanding AI search vs traditional SEO is essential for businesses planning their future search strategy.

Traditional SEO focuses heavily on rankings, keywords, backlinks, technical optimization, and search intent. AI search optimization still benefits from these fundamentals but places additional emphasis on clear answers, context, credibility, and content that can be easily understood by AI systems.

The best approach is not to abandon traditional SEO. Instead, combine strong SEO fundamentals with strategies designed for AI-driven search experiences.

Step 1: Understand Your Audience's Questions

The first step in AI search optimization is understanding what your audience actually wants to know.

Instead of targeting only short keywords, identify complete questions and conversational searches.

For example:

  • What are the best SEO services in Jaipur?
  • How does local SEO help businesses?
  • What should I look for in an SEO agency?
  • How can AI improve website optimization?

Tools such as Search Console, keyword research platforms, customer conversations, and analytics can help identify these questions.

Step 2: Create Direct and Helpful Answers

AI systems need content that clearly addresses a user's question. Avoid unnecessary introductions when a direct answer can be provided.

For important questions, provide a concise answer first and then expand with supporting details, examples, statistics, or practical recommendations.

For example:

What is AI SEO?

AI SEO is the process of optimizing online content and websites to improve visibility across search engines and AI-powered search experiences.

This format makes information easier for both users and search systems to understand.

Step 3: Structure Your Content Clearly

Content structure matters. Use descriptive H2 and H3 headings, short paragraphs, bullet points, tables where appropriate, and FAQs.

A well-organized page helps users quickly find information while making relationships between topics easier to understand.

For businesses investing in SEO for AI search, every important page should have a clear purpose and logical structure.

Step 4: Strengthen E-E-A-T and Trust

AI search does not eliminate the importance of credibility. Businesses should demonstrate experience, expertise, authority, and trustworthiness.

Strengthen trust by including:

  • Author information
  • Company details
  • Accurate claims
  • Reliable references
  • Customer reviews
  • Case studies
  • Original insights
  • Updated information

For commercial websites, clearly explaining who provides the service and why customers should trust the business can also improve the overall quality of the page.

Step 5: Use Answer Engine Optimization

Answer engine optimization focuses on creating content that can effectively answer questions in AI-generated and answer-focused search environments.

AEO strategies can include:

  • Question-based headings
  • Concise answers
  • FAQ sections
  • Conversational language
  • Structured content
  • Clear definitions
  • Supporting evidence

Businesses looking for AEO services should consider AEO as a complement to SEO rather than a replacement for it.

Step 6: Optimize for Conversational Searches

People often interact with AI tools using natural language. Instead of searching for "SEO Jaipur," someone might ask:

"Which SEO agency in Jaipur can help my business increase organic traffic?"

Your content should naturally address the context behind these longer questions.

This is one way how AI is changing SEO. Search optimization is moving beyond individual keywords toward topics, entities, context, and complete user needs.

Step 7: Consider ChatGPT SEO Ranking Carefully

Many businesses search for ChatGPT SEO ranking, but it is important to understand that there is no simple formula guaranteeing that a website will be mentioned by ChatGPT or another AI platform.

Instead, focus on the fundamentals: accurate information, strong website authority, original content, clear brand information, useful resources, and a technically healthy website.

The objective should be to build a website that deserves to be discovered and referenced—not to chase shortcuts.

Step 8: Monitor and Improve Your Content

AI search is evolving, so optimization should be an ongoing process.

Review your content regularly to identify:

  • Outdated information
  • Unanswered questions
  • Weak sections
  • Duplicate content
  • Poor internal linking
  • Technical issues
  • New search trends

Analytics and SEO tools can help you understand which pages attract users and where improvements may be needed.

Final Thoughts

AI is changing how people discover information, products, and businesses online. However, the fundamentals remain strong: create useful content, understand your audience, demonstrate expertise, maintain technical quality, and provide clear answers.

By combining traditional SEO with SEO for AI search, businesses can prepare for a search landscape where Google, AI assistants, and answer engines increasingly influence how users discover information.

Since the day of its invention, it has undergone constant change. Social media emerged as the next big thing on the Internet, with the goal of enabling people to stay virtually linked no matter where they were on the globe.

But now social media has transformed the marketing world, as it is the best way to reach out to people in no time. With the rise of digital marketing, social media has become a game-changer for organisations. You can sell or market anything and anywhere in the world; it doesn’t matter where you are located. 

So, what is social media marketing? 

In simple terms, marketing done over social media platforms like Facebook, Twitter, or LinkedIn is called social media marketing, or SMM. It might look easy, just like the definition but trust us, it is not. So, it is best to hire a social media marketing agency. 

To start anything, your “why” should be strong enough to motivate you to find the “how.”. 

Why do you need to hire a social media marketing agency?

Research

Make sure they are good at developing strategies as per your goals and should be able to run multiple campaigns simultaneously.

Creative and innovative 

Innovation and creativity are the cornerstones of social media marketing. Customers are more informed and astute these days; therefore, social media marketing companies need to go outside the box to draw in viewers. Should a campaign fail to provide desired outcomes, they ought to possess the ingenuity to modify their approach.

An effective social media marketing company produces captivating, unique content that appeals to the target demographic. They keep ahead of trends, create creative marketing concepts, and use narrative. They are adept with visual branding and storytelling, have a keen sense of their target demographic, and customise innovative techniques. 

Analytical approach 

To get insight into the demographics, interests, and behaviours of their target audience, a data-driven social media marketing business conducts audience research. They monitor performance indicators, spot patterns, and refine advertising. They compute ROI, measure conversions, and monitor discussions using social listening techniques like click-through rate (CTR). They offer thorough reports with practical suggestions for the creation of future strategies, and they continually optimise campaigns based on performance data.

Transparent SMM agencies set clear expectations for clients, maintain open dialogue, and provide transparency about campaign performance. They must embrace automation and artificial intelligence (AI) technology to simplify social media administration, increasing the efficacy, scalability, and efficiency of campaigns.

title: How do I find an SEO agency in India?

author: SMAC Digital
bodyHtml:
If you are looking for an SEO agency for your business, then you are definitely on the right track. It is well understood that digital marketing is the talk of the town these days and why not? It has opened the market to everyone, providing opportunities for every entity to compete equally in an unlimited marketplace.

Digital marketing is the soul of marketing, and there are many strategies involved in it, like social media marketing, email marketing, content marketing, and much more. Similarly, SEO is one of the pillars of digital marketing. Without these pillars, digital marketing agencies are unable to take a stand. Let’s check what exactly it is.

What is SEO?

SEO (Search Engine Optimisation) is a digital marketing strategy to increase your website’s ranking organically so that it appears in the top searches on a search engine page when users search with keywords related to your industry or product.

For instance, if you are a Jaipur-based manufacturer of bed linens, your website ought to show up on the first search engine result page (SERP) when people enter a phrase or the term "best bed sheet manufacturer in Jaipur" into Google or any other search engine. If your website appears in the first three to four search results, there is a good likelihood that consumers will visit it; if not, they will become disinterested or decide not to continue exploring.

That is why SEO is one of the most prominent features in digital marketing

So, the question is, can you implement SEO on your own? Well, it is better to stick to your forte and let the experts do what they do best. A seasoned SEO company can help in this situation. They are proficient in digital marketing and SEO techniques. Just like it's difficult to locate a pure white among numerous shades of white, you may find hundreds of SEO firms in India, but choosing the right one for you is not easy.

How do I find an SEO agency? There are many attributes of an SEO agency and other factors that should be taken into consideration.

Intent and Budget

Your primary goal is obviously to have your website rank higher in search engine results pages. However, how will it help you? If you are a new business owner, generating leads and building brand recognition may be your goals. Some may find that driving more traffic to their website results in more sales.

Each SEO agency will have a different price for each service based on their level of experience and knowledge. Thus, it depends on your spending limit, the services you want to use, and the SEO company you choose. Additionally, you may look at their pricing strategies, such as project-based, weekly, or monthly charges. Remember that some SEO companies could have really low prices, so be sure the company is well-known and established.

Explore

Once your intent and budget are clear, you can start your hunt for SEO agencies within your reach. You may get a list of SEO firms in your area, city, and nation by conducting a straight-forward Google search. The location doesn't really matter because technology has made the globe smaller as long as your goals are met, but it is always preferable to work with an SEO business that is local to you. After compiling a list of SEO companies, you are ready to conduct an in-depth investigation.

Check out the services and techniques

A good SEO agency should provide different kinds of SEO services and be capable of implementing various SEO techniques. A website’s traffic increases not only through content but also through different SEO techniques like on-page SEO, off-page SEO, technical SEO, and content SEO. First, you should be familiar with these terminologies and the SEO agency you are looking for should offer these services. An SEO agency should also be competent in link building to increase the website’s domain authority.

Apart from SEO techniques, you should also look for the analytical skills of the SEO agency. They should be able to provide metrics or analytical reports for SEO campaigns. Analytics is one of the most important aspects of SEO campaigns, as it helps track performance. There are many analytical tools, like Google Analytics, used by SEO agencies and you can look for those while digging deep.

Available resources

SEO is a challenging endeavour that calls for a variety of resources, including both technological and human ones. A strong team of technical engineers, website designers, content writers, and SEO experts should be available at an SEO agency. In each of their areas of expertise, they ought to hold certifications. It's likely that the SEO company won't be able to complete the jobs if their personnel don't have the necessary skills.

Portfolio

A portfolio is a great place to look for the SEO agency’s clientele. It gives insight about the clients who are associated with the SEO agency and which industry they belong to. It also provides information about the types of projects SEO agencies have worked on in the past and their accomplishments. A solid portfolio also depicts the professionalism of an SEO agency.

Client reviews and testimonials

Portfolios will provide you with client details and projects but client reviews and testimonials will provide you with the opinions of clients or what they feel about them. You can also connect with the SEO agency’s existing and previous clients and ask for more information, like what the agency did well, where they lag, or what you need to worry about. There might be some shortcomings, which you may or may not want to adjust.

Ethics

You will definitely want to make your website rank higher and you will get excited if an SEO agency gives you a guarantee that they can do this in a short time (one or two months). Well, this is a sign of an unethical SEO agency, as no one can guarantee the results in SEO.

There are some unethical practices, like black-hat SEO. You might get some quick results from that, but there's a chance that the search engine will block your website or you'll have to pay hefty fines. You need to understand that you need to invest both time and money on a long-term basis and there are no shortcuts.

Final discussion

Once you have identified the potential SEO agencies that fit your requirements, set up a meeting with them and set the expectations clearly. Make sure the prices, strategies, and KPIs are discussed. The SEO agency should be transparent in providing you with performance metrics as per the agreed-upon time frame and should be flexible to change the strategies.

title: Gen Z Marketing: A Guide to Reaching Out to Zoomers
excerpt: Some marketing experts say that Gen Z is a difficult nut to crack. Well, in our opinion, it is not difficult, but there is a different way to crack it. If relative processes and strategies are followed, they can take your brand to greater heights....
author: SMAC Digital
bodyHtml:
Some marketing experts say that Gen Z is a difficult nut to crack. Well, in our opinion, it is not difficult, but there is a different way to crack it. If relative processes and strategies are followed, they can take your brand to greater heights.

To start with, you need to understand the term ‘’Gen Z.". ‘’Gen Z’’ is also called ‘’Zoomers’’ and ‘’digital natives’’. So Gen Z is the part of the population that was born in the late 1990s and 2000s, and the age group they come under is mostly between 9 and 24 years.

The digital era, which gave rise to the internet, smartphones, and social media platforms, is when this generation was born. It is clear that they are more tech-savvy than their predecessors, the "millennials," since they were raised in the digital era. Conversations about the generational divide are widespread in our society, and it is easy to see why different generations face distinct difficulties and undergo distinct changes. These modifications have an impact on how they live, think, and view the world.

Gen Z is no exception, as they also conceive and perceive things differently. As they relate to things otherwise, the same old, outdated strategies are not going to work for them. Marketers need to have unique and suitable strategies to attract Generation Z.  

Why Gen Z?

Although Gen Z may not have the most purchasing power, they do have the most sway over millennials and other generations. Even though they may not have financial power at home, they nonetheless decide what 70% of the purchases are. They are more knowledgeable about trends, technologies, and current events. They participate actively in the economy and will be its main driver in the years to come. Therefore, it is essential that they have a unique marketing plan.
 

How do you attract Zoomers to your brand? Let us find out the important aspects of marketing for this new generation.
 

1. Values and morals:
The Gen Z generation is highly intelligent and socially conscious. Before accepting anything, they conduct extensive research. In addition to your goods and services, customers are searching for your brand's values, workplace culture, environmental sustainability, and a host of other factors when it comes to marketing. Even with the greatest items, there is very little likelihood that customers will interact with your brand if you lack any of these attributes.
When using social media for marketing purposes, be sure that your posts and advertisements really represent your ideals. Take a stance on environmental and social concerns that align with the principles of your company.

2. Transparency and Accountability
Zoomers are the most devoted consumers to any brand, but only after they perceive it to be open and responsible. People are seeking authenticity from you; therefore, you must first be open and honest about your company practices, the contents of your products, where your raw materials come from, and how well your goods or services work.
Gen Z strongly appreciates honesty; therefore, only make assertions that are true, whether they have to do with your products or any social issues. You should also take responsibility for your faults. Use user-generated comments and reviews wherever possible for your campaigns; they lend legitimacy to your company.
 

3. Entertaining Content:
Since members of Generation Z enjoy entertainment and having a good time, consider entertaining them before worrying about sales. Put another way, give them engaging and visually appealing content, which may not be essential for the product or sales.
You take it as an advantage or disadvantage; they have a very short attention span of around 8–9 seconds. So, you have to be very creative and try new ways of engaging with them. You can make short videos, reels, and some attractive Instagram posts. They like product videos; real customer testimonials and even educational videos are of great use. Do some research about their likes, dislikes, vocabulary, and demographics, and then use custom-made content for the group or individual.
 

4. Multiplatform strategy:
There are so many social media platforms available globally. Today’s generation uses multiple social media platforms for distinct purposes. YouTube for videos; Facebook for social networking; Twitter for microblogging; Instagram for sharing photos, videos, and stories; and there are many more platforms.
You need to apply different strategies to multiple social media platforms individually. The same kind of content can’t be used everywhere, as each social media network has its own specialty and users, and they like to see information in a different way.
 

5. Influencer marketing:
Influencer marketing is one of the most effective strategies for Gen Z, as they follow the influencers through various social media networks and platforms and trust them. You can partner with the influencers with their own expertise; for example, for the make-up brand, you can engage with a female influencer with expertise in beauty products. Today, there are so many gadget influencers that even big brands tie up with them for unboxing videos.
To engage Gen Z, schedule an influencer event for the introduction of your new product and promotions. It's not essential to collaborate with well-known influencers; you may also engage with nano- or micro-influencers; just be sure they align with your brand.

6. Deals and discounts:
Who doesn’t like deals and discounts? Zoomers are always looking for deals, as you can notice all big brands run specific campaigns for deals. It’s a great way to attract this young generation to your brand, especially when you are new to the market or have a new product launch.
You can partner with many brands to receive discount coupons, such as a coupon for a free movie, a discounted ticket to an amusement park, etc. You may also set a time limit for these bargains, which will help you prioritise them and also infuse FOMO (fear of missing out).

Nowadays, most brands are applying innovative strategies to attract Gen Z. Here are a few case studies of famous brands that show how they do it.

Nike

Nike's "Write the Future" campaign, which aimed to demonstrate how every action and accomplishment on the ground can alter people's lives, was one of the most significant FIFA World Cup-related advertising initiatives in 2010. They worked with well-known players and demonstrated their ability to perform in challenging situations. Due to Gen Z's intense football obsession, this campaign garnered numerous accolades in addition to increasing the brand value of the sports gear company.

Adidas

‘’Run for the Oceans’’ was a great campaign on sustainability; they collaborated with Parley to raise awareness about pollution in oceans and how plastic is a major part of marine pollution. Not only had they sponsored many big marathons and sports events during this campaign, but they also promoted the use of recycled plastic materials in their products. This is a great example of sustainable practices that attract Gen Z.


Dove 

The best illustration of authenticity may be seen in Dove's "Real Beauty" commercial, which features women of all ages, races, and colours. In addition to shattering taboos in the cosmetics industry, this brought the brand's principles to light. In addition to boosting sales, this campaign improved people's perceptions of themselves.

Coke

One of Coke’s most memorable campaigns was ‘’Share a Coke’'. People were crazy about this campaign, especially Zoomers, as it was more of a personalised one. It was a researched, planned, and executed campaign, as they had to choose names instead of the ‘’Coke’’ label. They tried to cover as many names as possible so that even if a person’s name is not there, it can be gifted to another known person whose name he got. This was a great strategy to attract younger generations, as it was more relatable to them. 

Conclusion

In the digital world, Zoomers are the trend-setters and decision-makers; they eat, sleep, drink, and live virtually. Therefore, you need to wow Gen Z with marketing methods that work for them if you want to build your brand and make future plans. Because online sales and promotions are the norm and because business is moving towards digitalization, Gen Z has been branded as the lords of the internet. You will gain from them if you value them.

title: Want to make your brand stand out in marketing and advertising world?
excerpt: There is a proverb by Matshona Dhilwayo: "Do what no one else can do, and you will become what no one else can become." This is the exact essence if you want to stand out in the marketing and advertising worlds. The marketing and ad worlds...
author: SMAC Digital
bodyHtml:
There is a proverb by Matshona Dhilwayo: “Do what no one else can do, and you will become what no one else can become." This is the exact essence if you want to stand out in the marketing and advertising worlds. The marketing and ad worlds are very vast and challenging because you are not the only one trying to make an impression. You have to compete with hundreds of brands that are in the same trade, and at the same time, you should be different from them.

Marketing and advertising are not only about selling your products; they are also about making connections with your audience. Even if you have better products or services but are unable to connect with the audience, everything is in vain.

There are many aspects of marketing and advertising that can make your brand stand out. Let us give you some important points to keep in mind to achieve your goal.

1.Individuality

You should, first and foremost, be unique; consider what sets your brand apart from competitors. The only person who can answer this question is you. Once you've located it, use your marketing campaigns to highlight its distinctiveness. Give an illustration. How do consumers purchase recently launched products before using them? The appearance, packaging, contents, colour selection, even the name and logo, are the responses.

2 . Values

Once you show your individuality, the next step is to determine what values your brand carries and what values you are going to pass on to your customers through your products and services. Values can be both tangible and intangible. For example, you could donate some money to local NGO from your sales or give a percentage discount to the first few customers.

3. Customer awareness

The first step is to determine who your intended audience is. Once you know your target audience, half the work is done. Now you need to be aware of and understand your target audience and customers. You can do research about them, their likes and dislikes, social influence, demographics, and much more. This will help you plan your marketing campaigns.

Now come the technical aspects or strategies you can use to stand out.

4. Innovation

Clearly, you need to be innovative in your marketing and advertising activities in order to stand out. With innovative concepts in the same setting as your rivals does not always mean that you have to do things entirely differently from them. For instance, you can begin with live product demos and feedback and then utilize the same for marketing and advertising.

5. Personalisation through analytics and AI

Customized marketing heavily relies on data analytics, and you may differentiate yourself from the competition by improving your marketing tactics using automation and artificial intelligence. You can implement personalized adverts based on their interests, past purchases, birthday/anniversary offers, etc. using various analytical and AI techniques.

6. Human touch 

Though AI undoubtedly aids in automation, human interaction is still crucial in marketing and advertising efforts as, at the end of the day, these are human interactions. Using storytelling to connect with your audience is a valuable marketing strategy. For instance, a commercial showcasing the effects of your products on customers after they use them, promoting the history of your business, or even a product narrative detailing the origins of the product. 

7. Collaboration 

Today, most brands do collaborations with influencers, celebrities, or cross-functional brands. Influencer collaboration is one of the most effective ways to stand out, but it should align with your brand's values and goals. The biggest influencers are your own customers, and they are the biggest offline influencers. You can collaborate with them; not only will it help you save some extra bucks, but it will also make your brand unique. 

8. CSRs and Sustainability 

Today’s consumers are very smart and aware; they are looking beyond your products. What brands are doing for society and the environment matters a lot to them. You can engage in CSR activities and even let your audience participate in them, but they should be genuine, not for name sake. You can highlight your sustainability practices or what you are doing for environmental safety. This adds value to your brand.

9. Evolution

As it is said, ‘’change is the only constant’’, it is critical to evolve with the dynamic world. Every now and then, the market is evolving with new technologies; not only do you need to be on par with them, but you also need to be ready for new challenges as well. You need to leverage the advancements in technology and marketing strategies. The more you are prepared, the more chances there are for you to be unique and stand out from others. 

In summary, in order to stand out, you must demonstrate your principles and have a thorough understanding of your target audience in addition to being distinctive. Thinking beyond the box will be aided by innovation; human touch, CSRs, sustainability, and customization will infuse your marketing and advertising initiatives with human values. Collaboration will assist in reaching out to more people, and all these processes and strategies will evolve with age as the evolution continues………

title: The Ethics of Digital Marketing and their Repercussions
excerpt: As you know, digital marketing is a way of marketing where marketing is done online through websites, social media, blogs, and advertising. As digital marketing is the way to go forward as it provides the advantages of ease of doing business, brand buildi...
author: SMAC Digital
bodyHtml:
As you know, digital marketing is a way of marketing where marketing is done online through websites, social media, blogs, and advertising. As digital marketing is the way to go forward as it provides the advantages of ease of doing business, brand building, and bigger outreach, businesses are engaging very quickly with it.

Everyone wants to take their business to the next level, and digital marketing companies help organisations fulfil their marketing goals through different digital marketing strategies. Irrespective of the size of the organisation, considering the ethics of digital marketing is crucial. 

Today, small or new brands are also giving tough competition to big and well-known brands because of digital marketing adoption. In this competition, there are many times when organisations are crossing the boundaries of ethics and fair business practices. For any business or organisation, it is very important to follow the code of ethics and morality for long-term growth and sustainability. If it is not done ethically, then the business can fall apart in no time.

In this blog, we are going to shed light on the ethics of digital marketing and its impact on your business.

What does ethics mean?

At first, we need to understand: what does ‘’ethics’’ mean? In simple terms, the meaning of ethics is the rules for doing things the right way. For digital marketing, there are certain rules or principles for doing it in an ethical manner. Let us go downhill and learn more about some of the important ethics.

1. Honesty and transparency:

As we know, there is a proverb: ‘’Honesty is the best policy''; it is a fact. You should be honest and transparent about your products, services, and business practices. You should only share or promote what your product has or does, and there should not be any false claims. Since your claims are based on reality, honesty in marketing will help you gain the customer's trust. Never make any promises that you can’t fulfil. If you are not honest and transparent about your products or services, you won’t be able to get new customers, and not only that, you will lose existing customers as well. Be transparent about your brand’s performance, sustainable practices, and digital marketing campaigns by making sure that they are not going to mislead customers.

2. Privacy and data security:

Lots of public information is collected during any digital marketing campaign, like name, DOB, email address, likes and dislikes, and many more. Make sure you have the customer’s consent to use it. You should be open about how the data is collected and used for marketing or analytical purposes. As you are collecting the data, you are equally responsible for data security. With the increase in cybercrime, protecting personal data is a major concern. You need to make sure that proper data security processes and policies are implemented and published on your website or in your digital marketing campaigns. This will create a lot of trust and belief in your customers and prospects.

3. Misleading and false information:

As it is said that this age is the ‘’age of information’’, well, it may be correct or false information. With so much information flowing in the digital world, it is very difficult to identify the authenticity of the information. With the growing competition and the appetite for success, some brands run digital marketing campaigns with misleading and false information. This may give initial success or monetary benefits, but the brand will fall down much faster, and it will be wiped out of the market. It is an obligation to market the correct information about your brand or product, make genuine efforts to reach customers, and take the criticism positively. It will help your brand grow in the long run.

4. Partnership:

When you are doing digital marketing, you need to make sure that your business or digital media partners are ethical and follow the same philosophies as your brand. It will not only increase your brand value but also your trustworthiness. Make sure to tie up with sustainable brands, as customers are looking for more than just products. A bad partnership or bad influence can harm your business, and it takes lots of effort to change the brand image. So, you have to be smart and aware when choosing your partners.

5. Audience sensitivity:

Marketers should be sensitive about the audience’s choices and beliefs. When performing target-based marketing, make sure that you are providing meaningful and likeable content to the customers. It is not advisable to overload the content or promotion with the customer or prospect, as they will lose interest and may not like your brand. When doing digital marketing, it is important to respect the faith and culture of the audience and not post anything that can hurt their cultural or religious sentiments.

6. Copyright and intellectual property:

Content plays a major part in digital marketing, like in SEO, social media campaigns, blogs, and advertisements. Nowadays, because of the increase in demand for content, some digital mark SEO,eting agencies copy the content and materials from other websites or social media. Marketers should use original and unique content for their marketing campaigns, as it will not only save them from copyright and intellectual property theft issues but also increase their SEO ranking and brand value.

Highlight the repercussions of disregarding digital marketing ethics right now

We have explained the ethics of digital marketing; it is equally important to know the consequences of not following the ethics. There are many repercussions to not being ethical.

  • The first thing that hits the organization or brand is losing brand value if you are doing deceptive marketing. People will lose faith in your brand and will never trust you again, even if you have started following ethical practices, as it takes years to generate faith and minutes to lose it. Not only can it affect your brand, but it can affect your industry as well.
     
  • Apart from the business side, there could be legal consequences as well. The customer can take you to court for misleading claims and wrong advertisements, and it will lead to a huge monetary loss. Even though there are huge financial penalties for copyright and data identity theft, it can also lead to legal confinement. Even unethical SEO practices can bring down your website, and it could be banned from the search engines, and there could also be heavy penalties.

Conclusion

As we have captured the ethics of digital marketing and the repercussions of not following them, it is very clear that following the ethical way is the mantra for long-term sustainability and growth. Marketers should focus on customer satisfaction, loyalty, sensitivity, and privacy. Be truthful, honest, and original in your digital marketing strategies. At last, we would like to say, ‘’slow growth with ethical means is always better than fast growth with unethical means’’.

AI is the hottest topic of discussion these days. Everyone is talking about it, whether they know about it or not. But what exactly is AI? AI, or artificial intelligence, is a computer programme designed to automate tasks that can be done through human intelligence.

AI was already there for a long time, like a simple calculator or a chess game on a computer. But now the advancement of AI has gone to a whole new level. The application of AI is vast, from asking to play a song to Alexa at your home to the assembly of vehicles in factories to the complex surgeries in operation theatres, and the latest one, ChatGpt.

Even the marketing industry is not untouched. With the help of AI, the whole aspect of digital marketing has changed. Everyone is interested in knowing whether AI will replace it or lead to job losses. In this blog, we are going to provide insight about the role of AI in digital marketing and its limitations.

Let us first take a look at the latest trends and uses of AI in digital marketing.

1 . Content Creation:

Content is at the core of any digital marketing campaign. With the use of AI, content creation has never been easier. You need quality content for your website, social media campaigns, SEO, email campaigns, etc. There are many content-based AI tools available, like ChatGPT and Jasper. If you want to create personalised, quality content quickly and at the initial stage of your campaign, then these tools will be a great help. A few examples of AI-driven content creation are personalised email campaigns, creating visual content, and optimising keywords for SEO.

2 . Personalization:

Today, we all see personalised ads, emails, and notifications. If we are looking for a book, we see all the information about the book in our browser ads, social media ads, etc. Without AI, digital marketing agencies also do this, but with AI, it is pretty much automated and fast. AI helps you increase leads, ROI, and brand awareness.

3 . Data Analytics:

It is a very daunting task when it comes to data analysis. We have tonnes of data today to analyse and act . One of the major advantages of AI is data handling. AI not only collects and analyses the data but also provides insights about your customer preferences, buying habits, and behaviour. With AI technologies like big data, you can plan your digital marketing strategies with focused investment. Data analytics through AI also helps in predictive analysis, like sales forecasts, web traffic trends, and the success rate of a campaign.

4 . Automated Customer Support:

Chatbots are a very useful AI technology for customer support operations. It is a real-time query-solving tool. Most businesses use chatbots for a better user experience. It provides round-the-clock support to your customers without a human presence. Users can ask anything about your products and services, and they get personalised responses. Hello AI, Lumen, and Nova are a few AI tools that are used for customer support applications.

 

As we have seen the advantages and uses of AI in digital marketing,  let us now look at the limitations of AI and what AI can’t do.

1 . Uniqueness and empathy in content

Although we have seen that with AI, we can get good-quality content for various usages, uniqueness can’t be achieved. A good quality of content is not that; it should be written in an impressive way, but it should have a human emotion in it. With the consistent change in algorithms of search engines, it is more important that content be unique and have a human touch; otherwise, it will have a negative impact on your online campaigns, like SEO. AI content always sounds robotic and repetitive. AI-generated content can’t produce creative ideas or content because it works on data that is only available. It does not have the ability to engage in critical and strategic thinking.

2 . Data Privacy:

Data privacy is one of the biggest concerns with AI. AI doesn’t discriminate based on the data it belongs to. Like the customer’s date of birth, you have that data, and you want to send personalised emails as per their date of birth. You are using AI for this task. You should have the customer’s permission to use this data. So when you are setting up an AI task, you should not break privacy laws. In some countries, data privacy laws are very strict, and it could land you in big trouble. You can collect the data through AI, but to use this data, you need human intervention.

3 . Human Connection:

AI can help you generate leads, but it can’t build customer relationships. Customer relationships can be built only with human emotions. You can use AI to automate tasks like sending emails to customers or sending promotions or special discounts, but they need a person to speak to when they reach out to you; they want to be heard and understood. Similarly, chatbots can automate the process of customer support to a certain extent, like providing answers to queries that are already there, but they can’t understand the user’s emotions. So, it works in synergy when it is used with the proper participation of AI and human intervention.

4 . Incorrect and biassed results:

AI works on the data that is provided or available. It does not have intelligence or judgment. If the data is incorrect, then the calculations and predictions will be wrong and biased. Therefore, AI can’t be used everywhere; the data should always be accurate, complete, and updated. If you completely rely on AI, then it can lead to incorrect analysis and predictions, and it can also target the wrong audience in your social media campaigns. AI-driven market research will work better when it is in the hands of humans, especially marketers or legit experts.

5 . Cost and implementation:

Implementing AI is a very complex task. You need a handsome investment to make it work. First of all, you need to have proper knowledge of the latest AI technologies and trends. You will need infrastructure and resources with the skills to support it. You will also need to train your existing resources to use AI. AI is an on-going job that continuously needs updates. So, for small and midsized firms, it is very challenging to keep it updated, as it takes a lot of time and investment. Instead of spending on marketing campaigns, firms will end up spending more on AI.

Please contact us for your digital marketing needs by visiting our website, www.smacdigital.com. 

Conclusion

AI definitely provides loads of advantages in digital marketing, but we can’t solely rely on it. AI works best with human intervention. When it is used with human skills like strategic thinking, innovation, creativity, and AI automation, keeping the shortcomings in mind, it will work like wonders in digital marketing.
